doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

chapter: Armstrong, the boats and the downtown halls
title: Wooden Joe on clarinet and how he switched to trumpet
summary: Martin first knew Wooden Joe on clarinet and made a record of him playing blues. Russell relates how an injury to his fingers pushed him toward trumpet.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: And you take, when I first knew Wooden Joe, he was playing clarinet. Yeah, I remember, I heard him on clarinet too. He played both of them in his late- You heard him on clarinet? Yeah, I made a record of Wooden Joe on clarinet that time. Yeah? He was playing clarinet. He played the blues, you know.

How he, from the understanding I got, how he got off of clarinet on trumpet, and he cut his fingers, cut his fingers, cut his fingers, cut his hand, and he couldn't... He could move the fingers, but he couldn't bend it.
That's right. Fingers like that stuff. Fingers like that stuff how he got off a clarinet on trumpet, somebody cut his hand, cut his fingers, cut his hand, and he couldn't...
Yeah, his fingers were stiff. He could move the fingers, but he couldn't bend it. He couldn't bend it. That's right. Fingers like that.
But he could still play clarinet a little, but not as well as they used to when I heard him.
